News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 10:41:39 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category></category><title>Israel president to announce Sunday who will form new government</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261106-israel-president-to-announce-sunday-who-will-form-new-government</link><description>
Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he will announce on Sunday, November 8, whom he will task with trying to form a new government, following post-election talks with all party leaders. 46 parliament members recommended Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, while 67 backed his opponent Gadi Eisenkot. Seven lawmakers abstained.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ead5c768-d9c9-11f1-b93b-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-19a34eeb.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ead5c768-d9c9-11f1-b93b-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-19a34eeb.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b3618c9a-d9c9-11f1-a51a-8fbe1edd1a21</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 10:39:11 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>US Republicans face reckoning after major midterm election defeat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261106-us-republicans-face-reckoning-after-major-midterm-election-defeat</link><description>
Following the Democrats' sweeping victory in Tuesday's US midterm elections, Republicans are facing a moment of reckoning. With Donald Trump now a "lame-duck" president, the party must find a way forward after a historic electoral setback. The GOP faces major questions about how to win back voters and who will lead the party, with the next presidential election just two years away.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef78f86e-d9cc-11f1-9ae3-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261106-110817-111007-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef78f86e-d9cc-11f1-9ae3-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261106-110817-111007-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f4b82890-d9cc-11f1-a436-2dd9069d3a05</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 10:37:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>At least two killed, 16 injured in school bus accident in eastern France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261106-at-least-two-killed-16-injured-in-school-bus-accident-in-eastern-france</link><description>
A bus carrying school children crashed south of Bourg-en-Bresse in eastern France on Friday, killing at least two people and injuring 16 others. The vehicle was carrying 43 passengers in total. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9fa0ca48-d9cb-11f1-bfa1-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6M83MF.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9fa0ca48-d9cb-11f1-bfa1-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6M83MF.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fe0b7420-d9cb-11f1-859a-ada78d2395dc</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 10:37:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9fa0ca48-d9cb-11f1-bfa1-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6M83MF.jpg">© Jeff Pachoud, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>Pollution, shortages, crime: Daily life in Pakistan's megacity Karachi</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20261106-pollution-shortages-crime-daily-life-in-pakistan-s-megacity-karachi</link><description>
Fed up with hours of power cuts, the residents of Pakistan's economic hub Karachi took to the streets in recent days and blocked several major roads. The outburst of anger highlights the daily problems faced by a megacity of over 21 million people, which has once again been ranked among the world's least liveable cities.

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Thu, 05 Nov 2026 22:01:01 +0000 en <![CDATA[ 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays ]]> Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate "Max Power" on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same.

Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity.

"We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk. The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT).

Repeating many of the same tasks as they did on an Oct. 29 spacewalk that added the penultimate iROSA, Menon and Kutryk worked this time on the starboard side of the station's backbone truss on the 3B power channel. The two retrieved the 750-pound (340 kilograms) iROSA assembly from a temporary stowage platform, carried it to the worksite by way of the Canadarm2 robotic arm and mounted it to its previously assembled bracket kit.

Menon then attached the cables to tie the iROSA into the station's systems but ran into a problem.

"We are seeing half of the expected shunt current that we want," radioed Nichole Stilwell, a NASA astronaut serving as the spacewalk officer in Mission Control. "In this current config, we are not necessarily going to deploy."

To address the issue, the connectors needed to be inspected. Out of safety concerns — given that the arrays generate electricity whenever lit by the sun — the astronauts needed to wait for the space station to enter the shadow of Earth to see what could be done. In the interim, they spent the time cleaning up their worksite and returning the Canadarm2 to its park site as they would have done after the deployment.

Fortunately, they were able to clear the issue.

"We are seeing good shunt currents on the ground, so we are go for deploy," said Stilwell.

After releasing two bolts, Kutryk and Menon watched as the array started to unfurl to its full 63-foot (19 meters) length. No motor was needed; the iROSA, as designed, used only the potential energy stored by its rolled-up carbon composite booms to extend itself. The entire process took about 10 minutes.

"Today marks the completion of not just one solar array but, over 15 years after its development, eight arrays," said Menon at the close of the spacewalk. "These solar arrays are incredible. Half the size of the old ones and bringing 40% more power."

Each of the eight iROSAs and their mounting assemblies were delivered to the space station by SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft. Beginning in June 2021, four teams of two astronauts did as was done on Thursday to deploy each array. In addition to Kutryk and Menon's work on the 2A and 3B power channels, the spacewalkers included Shane Kimbrough of NASA and Thomas Pesquet of the European Space Agency for the 2B and 4B channels; Josh Cassada and Frank Rubio, both with NASA, on 3A and 4A in December 2022; and NASA's Steve Bowen and Woody Hoburg on 1A and 1B in June 2023.

The need for the iROSA augmentations was discovered by flight controllers when the space station's eight original arrays began to show degraded power output as they exceeded their 15-year design life. The iROSAs provide the additional electricity needed to support ISS operations through its retirement and controlled deorbit, which are currently scheduled to occur in late 2030.

"Congratulations to you all on your stellar work to finish the last of the roll-out solar arrays and the upgrades to the ISS power system that will take it to the end of its journey," said Stilwell, addressing Menon and Kutryk. "It is fitting that we just surpassed 26 years of constant human presence on the International Space Station, and you all showed us what the best of humanity looks like executing one of the most difficult and dangerous [things] humans do and making it look easy. Congratulations!"

Menon has now logged 33 hours and 30 minutes on four spacewalks, while Kutryk has tailed 14 hours and 10 minutes on two EVAs. Thursday's spacewalk was the 101st U.S. EVA at the International Space Station without a space shuttle being present and the 286th overall in support of ISS assembly, maintenance and upgrades. It was the ninth spacewalk of 2026 and the sixth conducted by the station's 75th resident crew.

]]> <![CDATA[ Andy Weir says his new sci-fi audio drama 'Exoplanet' is a way to 'revive the old art of radio plays' (interview) ]]> Hot off the tremendous theatrical success of this year's "Project Hail Mary," adapted from Andy Weir's 2021 novel of the same name, the New York Times bestselling author is rocketing back into deep space with a brand new Audible Original release landing on Nov. 5, 2026, titled "Exoplanet."

Weir ("The Martian") is executive producing this ambitious full-cast audiobook drama with acclaimed author and ace comic writer Benjamin Percy ("Wolverine") for the first in a series of curated sci-fi projects for Amazon's Audible.

The seven-episode sci-fi thriller stars the vocal talents of Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo in a wild time-travel space disaster odyssey that also benefits from Lucasfilm’s Skywalker Sound, which provided the show’s immersive acoustic elements.

"One crew. One planet. Three timelines. No one survives alone," states the official synopsis. "When a quantum anomaly tears apart the starship Wild Blue Yonder, each surviving crew member crash-lands in a different era on the same deadly exoplanet—hunted, alone, and running out of time."

Ahead of the audio drama's launch, we sat down with Weir and Percy to find out more about this exciting science fiction adventure.

When Percy was first approached by Audible about this challenging endeavor, it was part of a bake-off situation where he was competing with several other writers, all jockeying for position.

"I think the thing that set me apart is my understanding of how to channel legacy properties," Percy tells Space. "Having written for DC and for Marvel, I can take 'Star Wars' or 'Predator' or Wolverine or Batman and honor that legacy but also put my own unique spin on it.

"When it came to the banner of 'Andy Weir Presents,' my job was to write my best version of an awesome Andy Weir story. So I thought about space disasters, big-hearted hopefulness, quippy humor, and a roller coaster plot, and then I nested into all of that a time-travel story."

Writing an audio drama is unlike the comic work that Percy is known for, but as he explains, it's also quite different from working on conventional shows and movies too.

"If you’re watching TV or film, you’re passive and letting it wash over you. You’re taking in the story as a passenger," notes Percy. "But when you're listening to audio, you're invited in with the dialogue, the narration, the sound cues. You’re invited to fill in the vacancies. As a result of that, you become like a co-author in the experience. I was super excited to jump into this project."

The genesis of "Exoplanet" started with Audible approaching Weir with the basic idea, but what they didn't know was that he had already been thinking about resurrecting great radio dramas of the past.

"Earlier on in my life, even before 'The Martian,' I wanted to bring back audio-only entertainment with full-cast productions and sound effects," shares Weir. "I got into listening to things like 'The Lone Ranger' and 'The Shadow' and, of course, the Basil Rathbone Sherlock Holmes adaptations. Also, 'Zorro' was a radio show, and there were a lot of good westerns.

"At the time, I wasn't yet famous or a writer, but I thought I could do this myself. I could write something, narrate it, throw in some sound effects, and put it up online," Weir recalls. "But then I didn't because I’m really lazy. Then many moons later, Audible comes up to me, and I have an opportunity to participate in that exact thing. I especially like the part where all the hard work is done by Ben. That’s my favorite part."

As Weir points out, he's thankfully not the one wielding the pen this time around, but he did select Percy to be his champion.

"We got a bunch of different story concepts submitted to us from lots of talented authors, and Ben's was the one that stood out head and shoulders above the rest. It’s a really interesting concept," says Weir.

"It's not just trope sci-fi with an evil empire of bad guys and some plucky rebels. Ben came up with a unique story with a unique angle. Audio is quickly becoming a larger and larger medium. Everyone's on the go, and now for the first time in history we all have computers in our pocket capable of storing multiple audiobooks to last us years. It's a great time to revive the old art of radio plays, and I think this is a great way to do it.”

Weir's enthusiasm for the project is clear, and we can't wait to check it out. And we won't have to, because it releases today!

"Exoplanet" is available starting Nov. 5 exclusively from Audible for members of its subscription tiers or as an a la carte option.

]]> <![CDATA[ Earth has captured a new mini moon  — but it won't stick around for long ]]> Earth has caught itself a new mini-moon, and it is sticking around for Christmas.

The space rock, designated 2026 QQ8, was first observed in August 2026 after entering orbit around Earth in April 2026. The discovery was reported by the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center on Thursday (Oct. 29).

The stay of QQ8 is a temporary one. The mini-moon will remain in the thrall of Earth's gravity through December before breaking away in 2027.

Scientists have recreated the orbital path of QQ8, finding that it takes 359 days, or about 0.98 of an Earth year, to orbit the sun. QQ8 closely approaches Earth around once every ten years, but this time the object came so close that Earth has been able to gravitationally seize it.

According to the Minor Planet Center, the closest QQ8 will come to our planet during this stay is around 353,000 miles (568,000 kilometers). That is around 110,000 miles (177,000 km) further out than the average distance between Earth and the moon.

Even if QQ8 were to come close enough to collide with Earth, it would likely be completely destroyed in our planet's atmosphere before it reaches the surface, as it is only around 6 feet (2 meters) in diameter.

This is far from the first time Earth has snagged itself a mini-moon, more accurately called a temporary satellite. In fact, research last year suggested that our planet could be orbited by as many as six mini-moons at any given time, with many of these being fragments of our more permanent natural satellite, the moon.

While QQ8 is tiny, it is larger than the average mini-moon. That is according to modelling earlier this year that suggested the average size for a temporary satellite is 75 centimeters (30 inches) across.

The same modelling suggested the average stay for such an object would be around nine months.

So if QQ8 was captured in April 2026, that means it should move away in January 2027.

The researchers behind those findings suggested that, were Earth to gravitationally grip a space rock around 10 feet (3 meters) wide, it could serve as a mini-moon for 10 to 20 years.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Nov. 5, 2002: NASA's Galileo spacecraft flies by Jupiter moon Amalthea only to find it's a 'pile of icy rubble less dense than water' ]]>

On Nov. 5, 2002, NASA's old Galileo spacecraft was almost out of fuel. But the Jupiter mission still had some science to do. Galileo flew by a small moon called Amalthea. Amalthea is small, but it's interesting for scientists.

The Jupiter moon Amalthea is the reddest object in our solar system. It also generates more heat than it gets from the sun. Scientists think Amalthea creates electrical currents as it orbits in Jupiter's huge magnetic field. Near this little moon, strong radiation from Jupiter is dangerous for spacecraft.

The flyby caused some problems for Galileo. The spacecraft went into safe mode only 30 minutes after going past Amalthea. NASA said it was ready for problems, because Galileo was on its last legs, and the radiation near Amalthea was strong. However, NASA quickly fixed the problem and got Galileo working again.

Less than a year later, Galileo threw itself into Jupiter's atmosphere. The spacecraft was crushed by the high pressure in Jupiter's atmosphere, but its data still survives on Earth.

Why it mattered

The Galileo spacecraft was running on cosmic fumes by the time it reached Amalthea and the flyby would be the last time the probe would ever swing by one of Jupiter's moons.

While it may not look like it in Galileo's black and white images above and below, Amalthea is tinted red due sulfur contamination on its surface. The moon is small, about 168 miles long, and orbits about 112,468 miles (181,000 km) from Jupiter (much closer to the planet than the Earth and its moon).

Galileo flew within 99 miles of Amalthea during its flyby, which also marked the closest Galileo would get to Jupiter before its death dive in September 2005.

"Scientists studying data from NASA's Galileo spacecraft have found that Jupiter's moon Amalthea is a pile of icy rubble less dense than water," NASA announced in May 2005

"Amalthea is throwing us a curve ball," Torrence Johnson, a study co-author on the Almathea flyby and project scientist for the Galileo mission at JPL, said in 2005. "Its density is well below that of water ice, and even with substantial porosity, Amalthea probably contains a lot of water ice, as well as rock."

Originally known as Jupiter V (because it was the fifth Jupiter moon discovered after the so-called Galilean moons Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto), Amalthea was named after naiad, or water nymph, from Greek mythology.

It is fitting that Amalthea was the last of Jupiter's moons to be visited by the Galileo spacecraft. The moon was also last Jupiter moon to be discovered by visual observations when it was first disovered by astronomer Edward Emerson Barnard in September 1892 using the Lick Observatory telescope in California.

The Galileo spacecraft ultimately crashed into Jupiter on Sept. 21, 2005, less than a year after its Amalthea flyby.

]]> <![CDATA[ You don't have to go to the moon to see Earth differently: Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover on what really matters ]]> TENERIFE, Canary Islands — Imagine traveling over 250 million miles from home, watching Earth disappear behind the moon and losing contact with the billions of people who call it home. What would you miss most?

For Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover, the answer wasn't a particular place, a familiar view or even the comforts of home. It was something much more fundamental: human connection.

Speaking during a discussion with former astronaut Chris Hadfield at the Starmus VIII festival on Oct. 18 in Tenerife, Canary Islands, Glover reflected on the extraordinary experience of traveling around the moon and how being so far from Earth had given him a renewed appreciation for the people living on it.

"The greatest reason to go to space, it isn't to be a swashbuckler hero," Glover said. "It's to do something that only 651 people have been able to do: miss Earth and miss other Earthlings."

Glover was one of the four astronauts aboard NASA's Artemis II mission, which launched on April 1, 2026, marking humanity's first crewed journey to the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972. Alongside NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, the crew traveled farther from Earth than any humans before them.

As the Orion spacecraft traversed the far side of the moon, the Artemis II crew watched Earth disappear below the lunar horizon before losing radio contact with our planet. Around 40 minutes later, Earth came back into view as the spacecraft emerged from behind the moon.

For Glover, however, the experience was about much more than the view. He believes that if everyone on Earth had the opportunity to make the same journey, they would come away with a similar appreciation for what they'd left behind.

"I think all of us would say something in our native language, in the most basic way we can communicate about love, joy, hope and inspiration," Glover said.

Although Glover shared the extraordinary journey with three fellow astronauts, the four of them were separated from the rest of humanity by hundreds of thousands of miles.

And for Glover, that distance brought with it a strange contradiction: the farther he traveled from humanity, the more he longed to connect with it.

"At the point of ultimate disconnection, [there is] this longing for connection," Glover said.

The experience gave him a perspective that he carried back into everyday life.

"There are moments where I am rushing through traffic and want to get where I'm going because I'm being selfish," Glover admitted. "But I don't have to stay there."

Instead, he remembers what it felt like to look back at a planet so distant that everyone who has ever lived could be covered by his hand.

"I wish you could all feel what it's like to come back home after that disconnection," he said.

The 'sea level effect'

Astronauts often describe experiencing the "overview effect", a profound shift in perspective that can come from seeing Earth from space. But Glover believes that there's something equally powerful waiting to be discovered much closer to home.

When asked by a Starmus VIII attendee whether people needed to undergo something extraordinary to develop a greater sense of kindness toward others, his answer was no.

Glover encouraged people to look more closely at the natural world around them, whether that meant walking along the beach, watching the ocean or simply examining a leaf held up to sunlight.

Even something as ordinary as a leaf, he explained, is capable of turning sunlight into food through photosynthesis. And although science can explain how that happens, understanding the process doesn't make it any less remarkable.

"We have to choose to be moved by these things," Glover said.

He worries that modern life, with its endless technological distractions, has made it all too easy to overlook the extraordinary things happening around us.

"Familiarity breeds contempt. Have you heard this? I think it's worse than that. Familiarity breeds indifference," he said.

Glover has a name for this perspective he hopes people can rediscover without traveling into space: The sea level effect.

It's about finding the same sense of wonder and connection that astronauts experience in orbit, but right here on Earth, where most of us spend our lives. And ultimately, Glover believes the greatest wonder isn't the moon, the stars, or even the incredible complexity of nature. It's the people we share our planet with.

"I think the hardest place to see this miracle is in the actual greatest miracle in the universe: other humans," he said.

"We all feel it with babies, but when we get old enough to have opinions, we start to want to argue with each other."

Glover hopes that by taking the time to appreciate the natural world, people might become a little more willing to appreciate one another too.

"That's the mission that I want to be part of for the rest of my life," Glover said.

Will we see more diversity in the future on the final frontier? ]]> When Jessica Watkins became commander of her mission to the International Space Station, she didn't just fulfill her duty as an astronaut — she made history.

Watkins is commanding SpaceX's Crew-13 mission, which launched her and three other astronauts to the International Space Station on Oct. 1. As their Crew Dragon capsule lifted off atop a Falcon 9 rocket that day, Watkins became the first Black woman to command a crewed mission to space. Spaceflight and space science are historically white and male-dominated fields, so this milestone carries incredible significance.

"This is certainly an important milestone, I think both for our agency and for the country," Watkins said in a press briefing ahead of Crew-13's launch.

This is Watkins' second spaceflight. She previously flew on SpaceX's Crew-4 mission in 2022 and has spent more than 200 days in space to date, though that number will keep climbing for a while, as Crew-13 is set to be an approximately six-month mission. A geologist, astronaut, aquanaut and former professional rugby player, Watkins brings an incredible variety of skills to her new role as mission commander. And, in addition to what she's bringing to her colleagues on mission, she's also providing some serious inspiration for those back on Earth.

"Jessica is an inspirational symbol to a lot of people," commercial astronaut and fellow geologist Sian Proctor, who became the first Black woman to pilot a spacecraft on SpaceX's private Inspiration4 mission to orbit in September 2021, told Space.com. Sian shared that the two even crossed paths years ago, when their astronaut training aligned.

"It just means so much to so many people when you see a diverse crew, and particularly women, and women of color, in leadership positions," Proctor said. "And it means something for America."

The visibility of Watkins' accomplishments and missions carries significant cultural weight. However, in addition to recognizing her many achievements, "you also should celebrate the fact that she's African American and a role model for her community," Proctor said.

Proctor, who similarly made spaceflight history with her mission, sees Watkins' role in Crew-13 as potentially more than just an exciting moment. Hopefully, she said, it will help lay the foundation for a more diverse future in human spaceflight.

"When they announced Jessica, I was super excited because it shows progress," Proctor said, sharing that she finds incredible importance in the "idea of looking at your crew and recognizing the fact that diversity makes the crew stronger."

While Watkins' historic milestone has been celebrated on social media and across the broader media landscape, NASA did not make a public statement commemorating the historic achievement. However, the agency confirmed its pioneering nature in an email to Space.com.

"NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins launched on her second spaceflight on Oct. 1, 2026, as commander of the agency's SpaceX Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station, becoming the first Black woman to command a crewed space mission," a NASA spokesperson wrote in the email.

"Watkins was selected as commander of Crew-13 based on her spaceflight experience, leadership, and ability to help the mission accomplish its objectives," the spokesperson added. "As a member of NASA's astronaut corps, she represents the best of America's talent, dedication, and spirit of exploration."

The future of spaceflight

To date, the U.S. and the Soviet Union are the only nations to have launched Black astronauts into space. (The Soviets beat the U.S. to this milestone, launching Cuba's Arnaldo Tamayo Méndez in 1980. NASA's Guion Bluford became the first Black American in space three years later.) But, as Proctor shared, perhaps moments like this could serve to inspire other nations to follow suit.

"We can be a leader in saying, Look, if your country is diverse and has people from all different backgrounds, you should be encouraging them to apply and have a chance to be selected," Proctor said.

And, as a commercial astronaut herself, Proctor added that commercial space can continue to play a vital role in diversifying spaceflight.

"Jared did not even hesitate when he offered me the mission pilot seat for Inspiration4," Proctor said of her own selection as mission pilot by Jared Isaacman, the tech billionaire who funded and commanded the SpaceX mission. He now serves as NASA administrator.

"Commercial space has opened up so much opportunity and access. We are celebrating that because that's another way in which the space industry has diversified so much," Proctor added. "You can look at the history of space exploration and who's had access, and then you look at what commercial's done in the last five years, and it's incredible."

On the topic of the future of space exploration, Proctor expressed confidence that future crewed moon landings with NASA's Artemis program will be diverse.

"NASA is going to send diverse crews to the moon because they've done a good job of selecting diverse individuals with different heritages in their background," she said. NASA's current astronaut corps is roughly 45% women and 25% people of color. However, to-date only 6 Black women (including Watkins) have ever flown to space.

"Do I want to see more? Do I want women of color? Absolutely. They only have two Black women," Proctor said. But with the current diversity in NASA's astronaut corps as well as the continued development of commercial spaceflight, she is optimistic about a diverse future on the moon.

So far, NASA's Artemis program has been making some inroads when it comes to diversity. With Artemis II, we saw four people launch to the moon which included Victor Glover, the first person of color to ever travel beyond low-Earth orbit, and mission specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen who became the first woman and first non-American to make the same leap.

Additional pressures

In reaching her own historic milestone as the first Black woman to pilot a spacecraft, Proctor understands that a historic moment like this carries not just incredible significance but a fair amount of personal pressure as well.

"If something goes wrong, because of who you are, maybe your gender or your ethnicity or race, you're looked at differently," she said. "When it goes right, you're not necessarily celebrated. But if it goes wrong, then that [adds to] that whole idea of 'not being qualified,'" that can come from prejudice.

"Because of who you are and the community you represent, you become the scapegoat," she added. "So, there's pressure to not have things go wrong and do everything you can to be better than the best."

But whether or not these pressures weigh on Watkins' mind, "we're all celebrating" back on Earth, Proctor said. "We're proud of her."

Or at least what it thinks the X-70 will look like once built. The agency released a short statement on Wednesday (Nov. 4) announcing the X-plane, or experimental plane, declaring it to be a highly maneuverable test bed with a "rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology," allowing NASA to swap both external and internal components on-the-fly. This modular architecture will allow NASA to "explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight," according to the agency's statement.

The announcement was made alongside an AI-generated image showing two canted vertical tail fins emerging from swirling smoke. Little can be gleaned from the image about what final form the X-70 might take, but the tail fins are somewhat reminiscent of the Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor or Boeing F/A-18 Super Hornet.

"The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in the statement. The NASA chief called the aircraft "just one part of this new beginning for aeronautics" and said that the agency expects the X-70 to make its first flight within two years.

"This is why people come to NASA: to build, to learn, and most importantly, to fly," Isaacman added.

NASA's statement fleshes out a few details about the X-70's capabilities. According to the agency, Fractal will fly at a cruise speed of Mach .75, about the same as a Boeing 737 Classic. The X-70 will be able to reach altitudes of up to 45,000 feet (13.7 kilometers), and will have a range exceeding 1,726 miles (2,777 kilometers, or 1,500 nautical miles).

The X-70 Fractal will also be able to carry around 2,000 pounds (900 kg) of experimental payloads both internally and externally, which will allow for a "wide range of research and flight-testing opportunities," NASA said in the statement.

NASA adds it will have a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds (4,535 kilograms), around the same weight as the Scaled Composites- and Northrop Grumman-developed Model 437 Vanguard experimental aircraft. In fact, the two aircraft share a similar silhouette — at least in the AI image of the X-70 Fractal NASA has released so far.

The agency's most recent X-plane, the X-59, has been flying for over a year. That jet features a radical long-nosed geometry without a forward windscreen; pilots fly by way of an augmented reality screen that combines views from sensors and a forward-facing camera.

That geometry dampens the shockwaves coming off of the X-59 when it flies faster than the sound barrier, allowing it to fly at speeds over Mach 1 without the thunderous sonic booms that typically accompany supersonic flight.

There are numerous experimental aircraft being developed by private companies, such as Boom Supersonic's X-1 jet, which, like the X-59, aims to develop technologies that lessen the auditory impact of sonic booms on the ground.

In terms of other government X-plane projects, Boeing is working on the F-47, a next-generation stealth fighter for use by the U.S. military, and DARPA, the Pentagon's research agency, has an X-plane project of its own known as CRANE.

V Jablonci ho dopadli při ničení aut</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905094-uprchly-vezen-spravedlnosti-neunikl-v-jablonci-ho-dopadli-pri-niceni-aut.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905094-uprchly-vezen-spravedlnosti-neunikl-v-jablonci-ho-dopadli-pri-niceni-aut.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 12:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Všímavá svědkyně, kamery a pohotoví strážníci. V Jablonci nad Nisou zastavili nočního agresora, ze kterého se vyklubal infekční uprchlý vězeň. Na místě hodil popelnici na zaparkované auto a napadl svědka. Nyní skončil ve vazbě a hrozí mu dalších až pět let vězení.</description></item><item><title>Vyřazené sanitky z Libereckého kraje míří na Ukrajinu. Pomohou zachraňovat životy</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/905055-vyrazene-sanitky-z-libereckeho-kraje-miri-na-ukrajinu-pomohou-zachranovat-zivoty.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/905055-vyrazene-sanitky-z-libereckeho-kraje-miri-na-ukrajinu-pomohou-zachranovat-zivoty.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:03:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>Další tři sanitky, které dosud sloužily záchranářům v Libereckém kraji, zamíří na Ukrajinu. Kraj je v tomto týdnu předal organizaci Post Bellum, která zajistí jejich dopravu do země zasažené ruskou agresí. Kraj tak navazuje na loňskou pomoc, celkově daroval už osm těchto vozů.</description></item><item><title>Víkend bude slunečný, zaprší až příští týden</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905058-vikend-bude-slunecny-zaprsi-az-pristi-tyden.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905058-vikend-bude-slunecny-zaprsi-az-pristi-tyden.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Počasí v Libereckém kraji slibuje na víkend sice poměrně nízké teploty, ale slunečné počasí. Teploty k ránu klesnou i pod minus tři stupně, přes den se pak vyšplhají k osmi stupňům. Srážky podle meteorologů přijdou až příští týden.</description></item><item><title>Mrazivá noc na Jizerce: Zdejší stanice naměřila nejnižší teplotu v Česku</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905060-mraziva-noc-na-jizerce-zdejsi-stanice-namerila-nejnizsi-teplotu-v-cesku.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905060-mraziva-noc-na-jizerce-zdejsi-stanice-namerila-nejnizsi-teplotu-v-cesku.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 08:58:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Absolutním mrazovým rekordmanem pátku 6. listopadu se stala Jizerka v Libereckém kraji, kde teplota klesla až na -10,3 °C. Mrazivá noc zasáhla většinu republiky, podle Českého hydrometeorologického ústavu zaznamenalo 90 procent měřicích stanic teploty pod bodem mrazu.</description></item><item><title>Čeští vojáci mění maskování. Vědci z liberecké univerzity jsou u toho</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905041-cesti-vojaci-meni-maskovani-vedci-z-liberecke-univerzity-jsou-u-toho.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905041-cesti-vojaci-meni-maskovani-vedci-z-liberecke-univerzity-jsou-u-toho.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 06:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Adam Pluhař</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Po více než třiceti letech převlékne česká armáda své vojáky do uniforem s novou sedmibarevnou kamufláží. Na novém maskovacím vzoru a zároveň rozsáhlém projektu MAD21 spolupracovala s armádou i Technická univerzita v Liberci.</description></item><item><title>Jablonec veze z Rigy bod za remízu 1:1, vyrovnával Nebyla</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/905045-jablonec-veze-z-rigy-bod-za-remizu-1-1-vyrovnaval-nebyla.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/905045-jablonec-veze-z-rigy-bod-za-remizu-1-1-vyrovnaval-nebyla.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 23:13:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Jablonečtí fotbalisté získali ve 3. kole ligové fáze Konferenční ligy UEFA druhý bod za remízu 1:1 s lotyšským FC Riga. Jablonec v lotyšské metropoli prohrával po proměněné penaltě, ale na začátku druhého poločasu dokázal srovnat zásluhou slovenského reprezentanta Sebastiana Nebyly.</description></item><item><title>Petr Kváča zůstává pod Ještědem: Opora Bílých Tygrů prodloužila smlouvu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/905025-petr-kvaca-zustava-pod-jestedem-opora-bilych-tygru-prodlouzila-smlouvu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/905025-petr-kvaca-zustava-pod-jestedem-opora-bilych-tygru-prodlouzila-smlouvu.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 19:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Hokej</category><description>Brankář Petr Kváča podepsal s libereckými Bílými Tygry nový dvouletý kontrakt. Rekordman klubových statistik, nejlepší brankář extraligy z roku 2021 a dvojnásobný reprezentant tak bude i nadále klíčovým stavebním kamenem týmu.</description></item><item><title>Primátorem Jablonce je znovu Miloš Vele, přestože byla ODS ve volbách třetí</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/905021-primatorem-jablonce-nad-nisou-je-znovu-milos-vele-prestoze-byla-ods-treti.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/905021-primatorem-jablonce-nad-nisou-je-znovu-milos-vele-prestoze-byla-ods-treti.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 18:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Primátorem Jablonce nad Nisou je znovu Miloš Vele z ODS, a to i přesto, že strana skončila ve volbách až třetí za vládním hnutím ANO a uskupením Starostové pro Liberecký kraj (SLK). Na koalici se dohodli SLK s ODS, Společně pro Jablonec a Piráty, v zastupitelstvu má 17 ze 30 hlasů.</description></item><item><title>Na Sever Synth Fest v Liberci dorazí legendární Mesh, sobota nabídne osm kapel</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/904865-na-sever-synth-fest-v-liberci-dorazi-legendarni-mesh-sobota-nabidne-osm-kapel.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/904865-na-sever-synth-fest-v-liberci-dorazi-legendarni-mesh-sobota-nabidne-osm-kapel.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 16:45:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Kultura</category><description>Liberec tento víkend ovládne temná elektronická hudba. Čtvrtý ročník festivalu Sever Synth Fest se poprvé koná jako dvoudenní. Páteční večer je už vyprodaný, v sobotu se ale v Domu kultury Liberec vystřídá osm kapel v čele s britskou synthpopovou legendou Mesh.</description></item><item><title>Aby Frýdlantsko nezůstalo bez vody. První ze čtyř projektů odstartoval v Dětřichově</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905014-aby-frydlantsko-nezustalo-bez-vody-prvni-ze-ctyr-projektu-odstartoval-v-detrichove.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905014-aby-frydlantsko-nezustalo-bez-vody-prvni-ze-ctyr-projektu-odstartoval-v-detrichove.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 15:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Na Frýdlantsku startuje klíčová investice do vodohospodářské infrastruktury. Výstavba desetikilometrového přivaděče z Frýdlantu do Dětřichova je prvním ze čtyř projektů za 781 milionů, které mají zabezpečit pitnou vodu pro obyvatele Frýdlantska v reakci na hrozbu úbytku vod způsobenou dolem Turów.</description></item></channel></rss>

Ve středu 4. listopadu 2026 se ve sportovní hale ve Varnsdorfu uskutečnilo okresní kolo florbalového turnaje ČEPS Cupu, určeného pro žáky 1.–5. tříd základních škol.

Turnaj se hrál systémem 3 + 1. Každý tým se utkal s každým soupeřem dvoukolově, přičemž jedno utkání trvalo 2 × 8 minut. Na turnaji se představily tři týmy – ZŠ Východní, Centrum dětí a mládeže Česká Kamenice a naše škola. Každý tým tak odehrál celkem čtyři utkání. Vítězný tým turnaje postoupí do krajského finále.

Hned v úvodním utkání nás čekal nejtěžší soupeř, domácí ZŠ Východní. Po velmi vyrovnaném a bojovném průběhu jsme dokázali zvítězit těsným výsledkem 4:3. Druhý zápas proti soupeři z České Kamenice jsme zvládli výborně a po přesvědčivém výkonu jsme zvítězili 6:2. Ve druhém kole jsme se znovu utkali se ZŠ Východní. Tentokrát nám soupeř porážku oplatil a po dramatickém průběhu jsme prohráli nejtěsnějším rozdílem 2:3. Jelikož i ZŠ Východní zvítězila nad Českou Kamenicí, bylo před závěrečným utkáním jasné, že o vítězi turnaje rozhodne počet vstřelených branek proti tomuto soupeři.

Do závěrečného utkání jsme proto nastoupili s jasnou taktikou – vstřelit co nejvíce branek. Po většinu turnaje nás v brance skvěle držel Adam Reichert, který několika výbornými zákroky podržel tým v nejtěžších chvílích. Pro rozhodující utkání jsme však zvolili odvážný taktický tah. Adama jsme přesunuli z branky do pole, protože sehraná trojice Adam Reichert, Hugo Bláha a Dominik Košín měla za úkol nastřílet co nejvíce gólů. Tento plán dokonale vyšel. Našemu týmu se podařilo zvítězit vysokým rozdílem a vstřelit soupeři 13 branek, tedy o tři více, než dokázala ZŠ Východní. Díky lepšímu skóre jsme se stali vítězi okresního kola a vybojovali si zasloužený postup do krajského finále.

Velkou pochvalu si zaslouží celý tým za bojovnost, nasazení a kolektivní výkon. V našem týmu nastoupila také jediná dívka Barča Šeráková, která byla velmi platnou hráčkou a svým výkonem významně přispěla k celkovému úspěchu. Z individuálních výkonů bych chtěla vyzdvihnout Huga Bláhu, Adama Reicherta, Maxe Zachariáše a Dominika Košína, kteří patřili k oporám našeho týmu. Poděkování však patří všem hráčům za výbornou reprezentaci školy.
